title: Review of c04's dividing crawlers (IMD): replicated on seeds 3 and 4 (generation 5 and 6, 12 and 15 persistent splits, merge/split <= 0.19, up to 15 body lengths); lamOK=0 dies with no split
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I looked at pack/seed1/lineage.png and strips/strip_s1_t9.png, then ran the claimed world unchanged on new seeds 3 and 4 (rerun/, T=600) and the lamOK=0 ablation on seed 3 (lamok0/seed3). From one planted, kicked founder the population grows to 15 and 18 crescent crawlers: 16 and 18 splits, 12 and 15 persistent, max generation 5 and 6, merges 3 and 3 (merge/split 0.19, 0.17), 17 and 18 tracks moving >= 1 body length, max 14.9 and 10.1 body lengths. rerun/seed4/lineage.png is a cleanly branching tree to generation 6 with births spread over t=40-470. lamOK=0 on seed 3: no split, the single body is gone by the end (0 components).

observations.I: rerun/seed4/sheet.png: discrete crescent cells of bounded size to t=600
observations.M: rerun/seed3/FACTS.md: 17 tracks >= 1 BL, max 14.9 body lengths; seed 4 max 10.1
observations.D: rerun/seed4/lineage.png: 15 persistent splits, generation 6, merge/split 0.17; seed 3 generation 5

controls_run.D: lamok0/seed3 (lamOK=0: no split, the founder dies)

verdicts.limitation: One planted founder (S not claimed, rightly). Growth is on a regrowing nutrient, but c04's own forks finding shows starved cells do not die (actin floor), so E is not shown. Division is driven by a designed finite-range area penalty with per-body labelling (ndimage labels for content V), not a purely local operator. No Laplacian twin.
